verses.122:2a: {ecce}, como os olhos dos {servi} * {inmanibus} dos seus senhores,
verses.122:2b: Como os olhos da {ancilla} nas mãos da sua senhora: * {ita} Senhor, nosso Deus, {donec} piedade de nós.
verses.122:3: Tende piedade de nós, Senhor, tende piedade de nós: * porque estamos muito {repleti} de desprezo:
verses.122:4: Porque a nossa alma está muito {repleta}: * {v4b}.

decisions.why: 'Ad te … levávi' is a formula of the psalter: 24:1 'Ad te, Dómine, levávi ánimam meam' is already 'A vós, Senhor, levantei a minha alma' (glossary, leváre row), and 85:4 and 142:8 have the same words. Against it stands 120:1, two psalms back, 'Levávi óculos meos in montes' → 'Levantei os meus olhos para os montes', where the Latin itself puts the verb first. The Latin line is sung alone as the Tract of the 3rd Sunday of Lent and the verse of the Introit of Monday in the 1st week (grep; ps122/circulation.md). The CNBB Liturgia das Horas (fetched) has 'Eu levanto os meus olhos para vós'.

options.label: A vós levantei

forms.adte: A vós levantei os meus olhos

options.note: Draft. The Latin's order, and 24:1's words for the same Latin (rule 6); 'levávi' kept as a perfect, as in 120:1. The pronoun that opens the psalm is picked up by the 'vós' of the second colon.

options.label: Levantei … para vós

forms.adte: Levantei os meus olhos para vós

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 ('Levantei os meus olhos para ti'), pt-PT and the CNBB order; would make the verse match 120:1 word for word up to the object. Refused because it breaks the 'Ad te levávi' formula of 24:1, 85:4, 142:8. If taken, the verse reads 'Levantei os meus olhos para vós, * que habitais nos céus' (the second colon then drops its 'vós', see quihabitas).

decisions.why: A relative in the second person, hanging from 'te' at the head of the verse, with 'óculos meos' between. In Portuguese the plural verb 'habitais' shows who is meant, but the ear meets 'os meus olhos' last. The clause is also sung alone as the Monday Vespers antiphon 'Qui hábitas in cælis, * miserére nobis' (Psalmi major, Day2 Vespera), where it has no antecedent at all. 93:2 'qui júdicas terram' is already 'vós que julgais a terra'.

options.label: vós que habitais
options.note: Draft. The subject hidden in the verb named (rule 2), as in 93:2; the antiphon reads alone ('Vós que habitais nos céus, * tende piedade de nós'). The Diurnal Monástico 1962 repeats the pronoun the same way ('a Ti, que moras no céu'). Same length as the Latin (7).

options.label: que habitais
options.note: Nothing supplied (the CNBB, Matos Soares 1932, pt-PT). Natural when 'vós' ends the first colon ('Levantei os meus olhos para vós'); after 'A vós levantei os meus olhos' the relative is heard a beat late.

decisions.why: ecce → eis (glossary, 133:1a). Here it opens a comparison that has no verb ('Ecce, sicut óculi … ita óculi nostri ad Dóminum'). Portuguese 'Eis que' is the standing biblical way to open a clause with ecce (72:12 'Eis que eles mesmos'); bare 'Eis,' before 'como' sounds cut off.

options.label: Eis que
options.note: Draft. The glossary's word in its usual shape; one syllable over the Latin's two, and the colon is still the Latin's length (10).

options.label: Eis
options.note: The bare particle, with the Latin's comma. Heard as an interjection with nothing to point at.

options.label: Vede
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 ('Vede que, assim como'). Turns the particle into a verb addressed to someone the psalm does not address.

decisions.why: servus → servo (glossary, 133:1a) and ancílla → serva (85:16 'o filho da vossa serva'; the word of the Magnificat and of Lk 1:38 in Brazilian use). The CNBB Liturgia das Horas has 'escravos … escravas' here (fetched), Matos Soares 1932 'servos … escrava', the Diurnal 'escravo … escrava': the image is of slaves watching their owners' hands, and 'servo' is softer.

options.label: servos … serva
options.note: Draft, by the glossary. Keeps the psalm's servants the same word as 'servus tuus' everywhere else, and 'serva' the word of the Magnificat's ancílla.

options.label: escravos … escrava
options.note: CNBB and the Diurnal (both from the Hebrew). The harder social fact; it would part these servants from every 'servo' of the psalter.

decisions.latin: sicut óculi servórum in mánibus … ita óculi nostri ad Dóminum
decisions.why: The whole comparison has no verb in the Latin, nor in the Greek. 'in mánibus' (the Greek εἰς χεῖρας, 'toward the hands') and 'ad Dóminum' (πρὸς κύριον) are two prepositions of looking. Matos Soares 1932 supplies 'estão fixos' twice; the CNBB 'estão fitos' in the first two members and nothing in the third ('assim os nossos olhos, no Senhor'). Rule 2 allows a copula the language needs; a participle like 'fixos' is more than a copula.

options.label: no verb

forms.ita: assim os nossos olhos para o

options.note: Draft. As the Latin: 'como os olhos dos servos nas mãos dos seus senhores … assim os nossos olhos para o Senhor'. Portuguese carries a verbless comparison in a psalm (the CNBB's own third member is verbless). 'nas mãos' against 'para o Senhor' keeps the Latin's two prepositions. Cost: 122:2a's second colon is 7 syllables against the Latin's 11.

options.label: estão (copula)

forms.ita: assim os nossos olhos estão voltados para o

options.note: A copula in the first member (the others follow it by ellipsis); the third member then needs 'voltados' to go with 'para', which is supplied. Brings 122:2a's second colon to 9.

options.label: estão fixos

forms.ita: assim os nossos olhos estão fixos no

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (the CNBB has 'estão fitos'). Familiar in Brazil from the Liturgia das Horas; 'fixos' is not in the Latin, and 'fixos no Senhor' loses 'ad', the movement toward.

decisions.why: The subject of misereátur is the Lord of the same colon; Portuguese 'tenha' is also a first person ('até que eu tenha'), though nothing in the verse invites that hearing. The CNBB antiphon for this psalm names him ('até que ele tenha pena de seus servos', fetched).

options.label: até que tenha
options.note: Draft. Nothing supplied; 'o Senhor, nosso Deus' stands just before. Matos Soares 1932 has the same.

options.label: até que ele tenha
options.note: The subject named (rule 2 allows it). One syllable more in a colon already two over the Latin.

decisions.latin: multum repléti sumus despectióne … multum repléta est ánima nostra
decisions.why: One verb twice, in the same words (quia multum repléti / Quia multum repléta), so one Portuguese word twice. The glossary's replére row gives 'estar cheio' (25:10, 64:5, 87:4 'a minha alma está cheia de males'). But 'estamos muito cheios de desprezo' is heard in Brazil first as 'we are full of contempt' — a feeling we have toward others — which is the opposite of the Latin (contempt suffered). 'Fartos de desprezo' can only be suffered: to be filled to the point of surfeit, which is also what πίμπλημι says, and the 62:6 row already gives 'fartar-se' to repléri (ἐμπλησθείη). The Diurnal Monástico 1962 ('Nossa alma já está farta') and the CNBB ('Estamos fartos do escárnio') both have it.

options.label: fartos … farta
options.note: Draft, from the Diurnal Monástico 1962. The repetition kept; the wrong hearing of 'cheios de desprezo' closed; the image (filled, sated) is the verb's. Departs from the replére row for this psalm: proposed in glossary.md (open).

options.label: cheios … cheia
options.note: The replére row (25:10, 87:4, whose 'a minha alma está cheia' is 122:4's nearest twin). Refused for 122:3: 'cheios de desprezo' is heard as contempt we feel.

decisions.why: The hard reading of the psalm. Two nominatives with datives, no verb, hanging from 'our soul is filled': DRB takes it as 'we are a reproach to the rich, and contempt to the proud' (we are that in their eyes); Matos Soares 1932 'de ser o objecto de escárnio para os ricos'; the Hebrew has genitives ('the scorn of those at ease'), which the Greek and the Latin do not. The dative can mean 'in the eyes of' or 'for, against'; the translation keeps the dative and does not choose. The Greek has articles (τὸ ὄνειδος … ἡ ἐξουδένωσις). abundántes of persons (εὐθηνοῦντες, 'prospering') → 'prósperos' (72:12, the abundántia row: 'abundantes' of people is heard as 'numerous'). oppróbrium → afronta (row); despéctio → desprezo, as 122:3 (ἐξουδένωσις, the family of contémptus, abjéctio, abúsio → desprezo); supérbi → soberbos (93:2).

options.label: a afronta aos prósperos, e o desprezo aos soberbos

forms.v4b: a afronta aos prósperos, e o desprezo aos soberbos

options.note: Draft. The plain dative 'a'; the Greek's articles. 19 syllables by checks.py (about 16 in the mouth, with a‿afronta, e‿o, aos) against the Latin's 17.

options.label: afronta para os prósperos, e desprezo para os soberbos

forms.v4b: afronta para os prósperos, e desprezo para os soberbos

options.note: 'para' leans toward 'in the eyes of' or toward 'meant for them'; heavier (21 by checks.py).

options.label: a afronta aos ricos, e o desprezo aos soberbos

forms.v4b: a afronta aos ricos, e o desprezo aos soberbos

options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and DRB have 'rich' (the CNBB 'ricaços'). Plainer; but it names wealth where εὐθηνέω and abundáre say ease and plenty, and parts from 72:12.

choices.122:1: No titulus: 'Canticum graduum' is not in DO's psalm file and tituli are out of the first edition (D7) — as Ps 133 and Ps 120. 'in cælis' plural → 'nos céus' (2:4 'Aquele que habita nos céus'). habitáre → habitar. The perfect 'levávi' → 'levantei' (as 24:1 and 120:1; the CNBB has the present).
choices.122:2a: dóminus of the masters → 'senhores', and of God (122:2b) → 'Senhor': one Latin word, one Portuguese word, so the image of the servant's master and the Lord is heard as the Latin has it. Second colon 7 syllables against 11 (checks.py), accepted: nothing is dropped, Portuguese is shorter here.
choices.122:2b: 'Dóminum, Deum nostrum' → 'o Senhor, nosso Deus' (apposition). 'misereátur nostri' → 'tenha piedade de nós' (the miseréri row), so that the next verse's 'Miserére nostri' is heard as the same words — the Latin's echo. The Missal's Tract (Quad3-0) has 'Et sicut' and later 'nobis'; the psalm's text is followed.
choices.122:3: 'Miserére nostri, Dómine, miserére nostri' → 'Tende piedade de nós, Senhor, tende piedade de nós' (the miseréri formula, plural; the same words as the Te Deum and the Preces versicle in the Latin). First colon +3 on the Latin, accepted for the formula. multum → muito, in both verses. despéctio → desprezo (see v4b). The vocative 'Dómine' bare, as the glossary's rule (no 'ó' where the Latin has none; the CNBB adds one).
choices.122:4: 'Quia multum repléta est ánima nostra' repeats 122:3's 'quia multum repléti sumus'; the Portuguese repeats 'porque … muito farto'. Subject-first order in the first colon (rule 2). ánima nostra → 'a nossa alma'.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps122.md. The Latin follows the LXX against the Hebrew in 122:4 (datives, not the Hebrew's genitives 'the scorn of those at ease'), and the translation follows the Latin. Hard readings: the verbless comparison of 122:2, the ambiguous datives of 122:4, and 'repléti … despectióne' (heard wrongly with 'cheios'). Precedents checked in the prayed files: 24:1 (Ad te levávi), 120:1 (levantei os meus olhos), 93:2 (vós que julgais; soberbos), 72:12 (prósperos), 85:16 (serva), 87:4 and 25:10 (está cheia), 66:2 (tenha piedade de nós).

Draft 1: hard pass. Soft flags: 122:2a second colon −4 (7 against 11), accepted — nothing is dropped, 'nas mãos dos seus senhores' is simply shorter than 'in mánibus dominórum suórum', and supplying a verb would add what the Latin lacks (see verbless). 122:3 first colon +3, accepted: the miseréri formula said twice, as the Latin. No rhyme or cadence flags.
